HISTORICAL SITE STELE OF THE REVOLUTIONARY YOUTH UNION OF GIA LAI PROVINCE (1962–1975)

Brief History:
In early 1962, the Provincial Youth Union office was established to mobilize and educate young people to unite, rise up against the U.S., and fight for national independence. When first founded, the Provincial Youth Union was located near Kpier stream; from 1972 to 1975, it moved to the central base area of the province (now Krong Commune, Kbang District).

Despite living and working under extremely harsh and fierce wartime conditions, every officer, union member, and youth of Gia Lai Province tirelessly strived, accepting hardship and sacrifice with the spirit of “Wherever youth are needed, they will be there; whatever is difficult, youth will overcome.” They successfully implemented movements such as “Three Revolutionary Assaults,” “Resolute to Win,” “Five Volunteer Campaigns,” and “Three Determined-to-Win Volunteer Campaigns.” These efforts contributed to the liberation of the province and the great Spring Victory of 1975, which liberated the South and reunified the country.

In April 2021, the Gia Lai Provincial Youth Union inaugurated the Historical Site Stele of the Revolutionary Youth Union (1962–1975). This site serves as a “red address” to educate union officers, members, and young generations across the province about the revolutionary tradition.
